key_insight: Nb and Ta preferentially segregate to grain boundaries in (Hf,Ta,Ti,Nb,Zr)B₂, linking group V bonding behavior to lower boundary energies and stronger interfaces.
engineering_relevance: Controlling grain-boundary chemistry could improve the mechanical performance of high-entropy diboride ceramics.
method: DFT calculations of four grain-boundary types in five binary diborides and HEB₂.
COHP analysis of metal–boron bonding at grain boundaries.
Monte Carlo/molecular dynamics sampling of six HEB₂ boundaries using a fine-tuned MACE potential.
evidence_signal: Nb and Ta enrichment reached 23–35 at.% at 2000 K across five of six boundaries; at 300 K, a segregated Σ193 boundary sustained 26 GPa in tension versus 20 GPa for a random boundary.
watch_item: These computational predictions require experimental validation, and the tensile-strength comparison concerns a single boundary type.
paper_title: Instability-driven segregation of V group transition metals on HEB$_2$ grain boundaries influencing enhanced mechanical properties
